title: Refusing to be polished into something else
odia: ମୋତେ ଯେତେ ମାଠିବୁ ମାଠ ମୁହିଁ ସେଇ ଦରପଡ଼ା କାଠ
literal_meaning: Polish me as much as you like; I remain that half-burnt wood.
explanation: The speaker declares that repeated efforts to change or improve them will not work. The blunt material image can make the refusal comic, defiant or self-deprecating. It voices a stance in a conversation, not a truth that people cannot learn or change.
meaning_odia: ଯେତେ ବୁଝାଇଲେ ବା ବଦଳାଇବାକୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟା କଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ନିଜେ ସେପରି ରହିବି ବୋଲି କହିବା।
usage_example: After repeated advice to adopt a more fashionable manner, someone jokingly insists that they will remain as they are. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The wood image and the first-person voice are preserved. This is distinct from enduring pressure: here the emphasis falls on resisting another person’s attempts to remake the speaker. The source spells the word ଦରପଡ଼ା. “Half-burnt” is an editorial interpretation of that spelling, not a verified correction to the original; lexical and human review remain pending.
